newsitem.title: USA: Harken drilling second Rio Negro effort.
newsitem.headline: Harken drilling second Rio Negro effort.

text.p: Harken Energy Corp said Tuesday it has begun drilling operations on the Torcaz 3 well on the Rio Negro prospect in Colombia.

The drillsite was identified through seismic analysis and subsurface data from previous wells drilled nearby, including the Rio Negro discovery well, the Torcaz 2, which the company was unable to test because of formation damage. The well did provide valuable engineering and geological data that will be used in the drilling and completion of Torcaz 3, Harken said.
Marlin Drilling Co, a subsidiary of Pride Petroleum Services Inc, has been contracted to drill the well.
The company said the Torcaz 3 well is expected to reach a depth of about 8,000 feet and will take about 30 days to drill and an additional 30 days to test and evaluate.
Harken said the well should test two oil-prone zones prevalent in the Middle Magdalena Basin -- the Mugrosa and Esmeraldas formations.
"We are anxious to test a modified completion technique at Torcaz 3," Chairman Mikel Faulkner said.
"We are hopeful it will increase the potential value of reserves already identified at Rio Negro."

He also said "The remainder of 1997 will be very busy for us in Colombia. We plan to drill three significant exploratory prospects, to acquire and process new seismic data, to obtain a new Association contract area and to continue the development of the Rio Negro and the Palo Blanco prospects."
